title: Formal Security of the Always-PMAC OCB2 Variant
summary: Preliminary analysis finds the empty-input PMAC value unpredictable and non-replayable, but formal authenticated-encryption security of the repaired OCB2 remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: In OCB2, the value $\mathsf{PMAC}(A)$ computed on associated data $A$ is XORed into the authentication tag only when $A\neq\varepsilon$. Consider the modified variant that removes this condition and always XORs $\mathsf{PMAC}(A)$ into the tag, including when $A=\varepsilon$. Initial analysis indicates that $\mathsf{PMAC}(\varepsilon)$ is unpredictable and cannot be replayed from other ciphertexts. Establish or refute a formal authenticated-encryption-with-associated-data security theorem for this modified OCB2 variant, explicitly covering both $A=\varepsilon$ and $A\neq\varepsilon$.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptography, focusing on authenticated encryption and PMAC-based authentication in OCB2.
parameters: A: associated data input, with empty and nonempty cases
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish or refute a formal authenticated-encryption-with-associated-data security theorem for the modified OCB2 variant, covering both empty and nonempty associated data.

citations.label: Cryptanalysis of OCB2: Attacks on Authenticity and Confidentiality

progress.summary: The source presents always including PMAC on associated data, including empty data, as an OCB2 repair. It reports preliminary evidence of unpredictability and non-replayability for the empty case but leaves the repair's formal security theorem unproved.
citation_labels: Akiko Inoue et al., Cryptanalysis of OCB2: Attacks on Authenticity and Confidentiality
